chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Qarin narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Hsinjani narrated to us, saying: Sadir narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Najran narrated to us that Abu al-Khalid narrated to him and swore to him upon it,
This nation will not be destroyed until there are twelve Caliphs among them, all of whom act according to guidance and the true religion.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the twelve Caliphs in Shia eschatology and governance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal conveys a prophecy regarding the twelve Caliphs (or leaders) who will lead the Muslim community after the Prophet. It asserts that the nation will not perish as long as these twelve leaders govern according to divine guidance and the true religion, emphasizing the continuity of legitimate leadership. In Shia scholarship, this is often linked to the concept of the Twelve Imams, with the final Imam being in occultation, ensuring the preservation of the faith until the Day of Resurrection.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 12-33 Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Qat’tan narrated that Muhammad ibn Qarin quoted Ali ibn al-Hassan al-Hisinjany, on the authority of Sadir, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Najran that Abal Khalid swore and said,
“This nation will not be destroyed until there comes twelve Caliphs all of whom act according to guidance and the true religion.”
